title: Rooms needed
statement:
An office has meetings given as `[start, end]` times. A meeting occupies a room from `start` up to but not including `end`, so a meeting ending at 10 and another starting at 10 can share a room.

Return the smallest number of rooms needed to hold every meeting.

clarifyingQuestions.question: If one meeting ends at 10 and another starts at 10, can they share a room?

edgeCases.why: One room suffices because ends are exclusive.

edgeCases.input: All start at the same time
One long meeting with short ones inside

approaches.name: Check every time point
approaches.idea: For every start time, count meetings in progress.

approaches.name: Sort by start, min-heap of end times
approaches.idea: Process meetings by start time, keeping a heap of end times for rooms in use. If the earliest-ending room is free by this start, reuse it; otherwise add a room.

approaches.name: Two sorted lists sweep
approaches.idea: Sort starts and ends separately and sweep: each start takes a room, each end that is at or before the current start frees one. Track the maximum in use.

optimal.name: Sort plus min-heap of end times
optimal.explanation: Sort meetings by start. For each, if the heap’s smallest end is <= start, replace it with this meeting’s end (reuse that room); otherwise push this end (new room). The heap size at the end is the number of rooms.

hintLadder: When a meeting starts, which room is the best one to try to reuse?
How can you always know which room frees up first?
Process meetings in order of start time.
Sort by start and keep a min-heap of end times; reuse the room at the top if it is free.

expectedMentions.what: Asks whether a meeting ending at t frees the room for one starting at t
Proposes sorting by start with a min-heap of end times, O(n log n)
Explains why reusing the earliest-ending room is safe
Traces the example or back-to-back meetings

followUps: Return which room each meeting goes to.
Rooms have capacities and meetings have sizes.

walkthrough.say: A meeting ending at 10 and one starting at 10 can share a room? And the meetings aren’t sorted?

I’ll go through meetings in order of start time and track rooms in use by their end times. When a meeting starts, the room most likely to be free is the one that ends earliest, so a min-heap of end times fits. If that earliest end is at or before the start, reuse it; otherwise open a new room.
Sorting is n log n and each heap operation is log n, so O(n log n) overall, O(n) space.
heapreplace pops the smallest and pushes the new end in one step.

Example sorted: 9-12, 10-11, 11-13, 12-14. 9-12 opens room one. 10-11: earliest end is 12, not free, room two. 11-13: earliest end is 11, free, reuse. 12-14: earliest end is 12, free, reuse. Two rooms.
Back to back 1-2, 2-3, 3-4: each start equals the earliest end, so they all reuse one room. That’s the less-than-or-equal mattering.
O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
